templates_considered: RET-002: retained data has a cleanup task. Fits the 2-year retention ask. Used as-is, tags set to retained
RET-001: only the audit function writes the audit log. Not asked; audit_log already written only by record_audit_event
DATA-010: endpoints don't return personal data. Relevant to GDPR but not to deletion or retention; left out to keep to the ask
CONF-011 / CONF-012: sensitive field marking and table tagging. Not asked; would need every personal field named first
LOG-001: logs don't contain personal data. Not asked
AUTH-010: endpoints require login. Not asked; account DELETE already uses auth = users

Erase and expire personal data recipe (GDPR): fits the ask. Used its erasure rule as an extra rule in GDPR-ERASE-001, with its table_selector changed to has_fk_to users, since the workspace has no personal tag

rules.covers: 2-year retention: each table holding retained data has a scheduled task that deletes from it (age not checked)
account deletion everywhere: every table with a foreign key to users is deleted from by a function tagged erasure

ask_parts_not_covered.part: Keep no customer data longer than 2 years: the age at which rows are deleted
Customer data linked by org or customer rather than user (customers, invoices, payments, payment_method, patients, orders via customer_id)
ask_parts_not_covered.why: couldn't tell how: no user link on these tables, so the rule cannot tell whose rows they are

ask_parts_not_covered.part: Deletion actually carried out in backups, logs, vendors (card processor, email, AI providers) and copies
GDPR compliance as a whole, including deletion requests handled in time

assumptions: The erasure function is delete_user_account (called by DELETE /account); I assumed it should carry the erasure tag
Tables with a user link are those with a foreign key to users in the pulled schema: orders, support_tickets, sessions, user_address
retained is the tag RET-002's template uses for tables on a cleanup schedule
The customer means the end users of the consumer app (users table) when they say user; the customers table is B2B-org-linked so I did not treat it as personal data for the account-deletion rule
confusions: Tables in the pulled workspace carry no tags at all, yet RET-002 and the GDPR recipe both tell me to tag tables first. The skill says a warning about a missing tag means the rule judges nothing and to propose the tag separately, but a 'proposed' tag is the only way the rule can ever judge anything. The guidance does not say how to ship a policy that is correct but inert until tags are added

The recipe's erasure rule is written for a table tagged personal, but the skill's catalogue also says tables are selected by has_fk_to inside table_selector. I did not find an example that combines has_fk_to with referenced_by, so I combined them from the param description alone
I did not read kit/catalogue.json in full (it is very large); I used the skill's catalogue text and the template summaries. The param names I used came from the skill, not the JSON
Working directory moved mid-run from the project root to ./workspace; I used absolute paths for out/ to avoid writing into the pulled workspace
Whether a table with a foreign key to users but no rows of a person should be counted as covered is not stated
wished_for: A worked example of table.coverage_required with table_selector.has_fk_to plus referenced_by, to confirm the param shape
A recipe for linking org-scoped data (customers, invoices) to a person for erasure, since no user link exists on those tables
A way to express a retention age, even as a documented 'the task deletes rows older than N days' check, or at least a note on how to record the period
A template or check telling the team to tag existing tables and functions as a first step before tag-based rules judge anything, with a short list of tags to propose
parse_errors_seen: RET-002.R1: tags "retained" is on no table on this branch, so it selects nothing (warning, not error)
GDPR-ERASE-001.R1: referenced_by.tags "erasure" is on no function on this branch (warning, not error)
why_confidence: The erasure rule covers the user-linked tables, but only once the erasure tag exists on delete_user_account, and the current function already misses orders and support_tickets. The 2-year limit is not checkable at all: RET-002 only confirms a cleanup task exists. Customer rows linked by org have no user link, so erasure cannot cover them. Neither policy is compliance evidence.
